summary: This core is built like the board. Video timing comes from H/V counters addressing the board's timing PROMs (ROM14/ROM15). The tile layers are 8-bit shift registers with S0/S1 load/shift-left/shift-right modes and colour latches clocked at tile boundaries. The sprite engine is a PROM-sequenced pipeline (ROM16/17/18) feeding a per-line sorting RAM, then ping-pong 6148 line buffers whose write enables are spelled out as individual gates (S2_U7M, S2_U8M, S2_U1R...). Nothing follows MAME's draw_slapfight_sprites loop, its tilemap callbacks or its buffered-spriteram/periodic-NMI abstractions. The only MAME-like traces are a behavioural FG>SP>BG priority if/else and a few blanking/offset constants that resemble MAME's.

findings.where: rtl/slapcore/slapcore.v:122-137,198-213 (ROM15 U8B, ROM14 U2C); rtl/slapcore/ROM82S129sv.sv module ROM14
findings.note: The H and V counters address the PROM dumps ROM14/ROM15. PROM output bits supply counter reset, HSYNC, HBLANK, VSYNC and VBLANK, latched on the line clock the way the board's PROM decode works. MAME just uses fixed screen parameters.

ROM18 drives a control latch (LS175 style). Counter-addressed ROM16/ROM17 produce a 3-bit command decoded into latch strobes (LAT_HPOS/XDAT/VPOS/INDX) that are ORed with the pixel clock. MAME's version is a for-loop over 0x800 bytes calling gfx->transpen.

findings.signal: Gate- and flip-flop-level sprite logic with chip-location names
findings.note: Individual LS74 halves (S2_U7BA/U7BB with preset/clear) and NOR/NAND nets (S2_U4C_*, S2_U7M_*, S2_U8M_*, S2_U1R_*, S2_U1T_*) build the 32K RAM control and the line-buffer /WE signals. This is netlist-style logic named after board positions.

findings.signal: Per-line sprite sorting RAM and ping-pong 6148 line buffers
findings.note: Sprite attributes are written into a RAM indexed by VPOS and an incrementing high nibble kept in a 6148 (S2_U2F). A loadable down-counter (LNBF_CNT) addresses two line buffers (S2_U5T/S2_U5M), which swap on CPU_RAM_SYNC. This is the board's scan-time pipeline, not a per-frame draw.

FG_SYNC/BG_SYNC come from XOR/AND of HPIX bits 0-2 with the flip signal. These drive S0/S1 mode pins of 8-bit shift registers (load, shift left, or shift right when flipped), and the colour attribute is latched on a derived colour_copy clock. MAME's tilemap callbacks do not work this way.

findings.signal: Video-RAM wait states MAME does not model
findings.note: When the CPU selects video RAM, a shift register clocked by the tile clock (FG_CLK/BG_CLK) inserts Z80 WAIT cycles. This is bus-contention behaviour of the real board, and the MAME driver has nothing like it.

findings.signal: Sound NMI from a counter and shared RAM over BUSRQ
findings.note: The audio NMI is bit 12 or bit 13 of a 14-bit counter (U7A_TMR) clocked at 3 MHz. The main CPU reaches sound RAM by asserting the audio Z80's BUSRQ and muxing the address bus on BUSAK. MAME uses a 360/180 Hz periodic interrupt and a plain shared RAM.

findings.signal: Discrete active-low address decode and A0-data I/O latch
findings.note: Chip selects are ORs of MREQ with address bits, and the I/O latch stores A0 as data, indexed by A3:A1. Signal names (U9J_Q5, IO_C_SPRITE_COLOUR, RESET_68705) are board nets, not MAME handler names. The memory map itself is neutral.

Layer priority is an if/else on non-zero pixels (FG > sprite > BG) that matches MAME's draw order. It is not expressed as the board's gating or PROM. This is a weak signal; a correct core needs the same outcome.

findings.signal: Offset and blanking constants similar to MAME's
findings.note: H_BLANK trims at HPIX<13 or >283, and the vertical offsets are 16/8 with a -16 flip tweak. These look like empirical display adjustments; 13/284 sit close to MAME's sprite offsets. They are minor and do not affect the overall structure.

findings.signal: Clock enables from 48 MHz and BRAM ROMs
findings.note: Clock enables derived from a 48 MHz counter and dual-port BRAM standing in for the 6116/2016 RAMs are normal FPGA engineering.
